svg.text: COPPER SIDE, mirrored: what you see when you cut the tracks
18 × 14 holes · cut to 45.7 × 35.6 mm · 5 cuts · 3 links · 2 standoff holes (2.5 mm, for M2.5 nylon standoffs)
Take 9 V from the barrel or the battery, protect it, and hand it to the codec carrier.
D1 1N5817 — band towards the right, the cathode
R11 680k — the battery meter, top resistor
Connectors (pin 1 is the large filled square)
P2 → DC socket, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 +9 V · 3 the switch lug:
P1 → Codec carrier, JST-XH 2-way (B2B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 +9 V
P4 → Control: Pico 2 WH, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 VBAT · 2 VDC · 3 —
No ground: a high-value resistor at the power end of each wire; the
GND reaches the root through P1 only (Codec carrier).
The sleeve is +9 V and the centre pin is 0 V: the Cioks outlet is
centre-negative. Confirm the socket with a meter before trusting the lugs.
With no plug in, the socket's switch joins the SW lug to the sleeve, so the
battery feeds the diode. A plug opens the switch. The board does not join
One diode protects both sources. The battery plug is 3-way, so it cannot go
No filter here. The 9 V leaves protected and unfiltered; the input board
The two sense wires carry no ground. Each has its resistor at this end, and
the few microamps return through the tree. The bottom resistors and the
capacitors are on the control board.

Red ✕: cut the track at that hole (red bar: cut between two holes). Lines: wire links on the component side (green carries ground). Strips tinted green carry ground, red a supply, amber 3.3 V. White circles: standoff holes; dashed: what the standoff covers.
